idiom_name: Koin module DSL with constructor references (singleOf/factoryOf) + get()/inject()
implementation_notes: The consumer side is plain Kotlin - primary-constructor parameter properties declare dependencies (class Service(private val repo: Repo)) - and Koin supplies the injector: definitions are registered in a module DSL (singleOf(::Repo), factory, viewModel) with constructor references auto-wired, and resolved with get()/inject() or by delegate. With the Kotlin 2.x Compiler Plugin, Koin also validates the graph at build time and generates the wiring. What replaces the classic injector/config structure is this module DSL; hand-written primary-constructor wiring remains the zero-framework baseline.
pitfalls: Default parameter values confuse Koin autowiring: every constructor parameter is resolved, so defaults are not fallbacks.
kotlin `object` singletons masquerade as injected services and keep a global lifetime - inject an interface instead.
Koin's Compiler Plugin or classic DSL must match the Kotlin version; a missing plugin leaves get() paths unverified.

variants.name: Hilt/Dagger generated component (Android)
variants.implementation_notes: Hilt layers Android lifecycle components over Dagger: modules installed with @InstallIn(SingletonComponent::class) provide bindings (@Provides, scoped with @Singleton/@ActivityScoped) and @Inject on a constructor both requests injection and tells Hilt how the type is created. Everything is generated at compile time, so the graph is validated during the build with no reflection; the cost is annotation processing, generated code and Android-specific component scopes. Choose it for Android apps; Koin or kotlin-inject fit multiplatform and backend code better.
pitfalls: Providers can only inject bindings visible to the same component; a wrong @InstallIn target produces compile-time Dagger errors that name generated types.
A binding scoped with an annotation the target component does not support fails the build - match scope to component.

variants.name: kotlin-inject compile-time component (multiplatform)
variants.implementation_notes: kotlin-inject is a compile-time, multiplatform DI library: an @Component abstract class or interface declares what is exposed, @Provides members supply external or third-party types, and @Inject on a class makes its primary constructor the provider - the KSP-generated implementation wires the whole graph without reflection. It is the multiplatform answer to Dagger (Hilt is Android-only) and works for backend/library code too. Prefer it when compile-time safety and no runtime dependency matter; Koin is friendlier for rapid DSL-based setup.
pitfalls: KSP must run before compilation; a stale or missing generated component breaks both build and IDE navigation.
Component-scoped instances need the right scope annotation, otherwise every resolution creates a new object.
